label: Glassflow
Show settings for *Pick one part at a time, or Everything. Settings keep their values while hidden.*
Colour
Colour source *Container colour is read from the tab itself, so tabs in different containers differ. Tabs with no container use the fallback below.*
Fallback colour *Used when a tab has no container, no folder, or the workspace has no colour set.*
Custom colour *Any CSS colour. Used when source or fallback is set to Custom.*
Darkness *Mixes the source toward black. 0% keeps Zen's pastel hue, 45% is a deep jewel tone.*
Second gradient colour *Used by gradients whose end is set to 'Fade to a second colour'.*
Glass
Glass intensity *Scales every sheen, rim and glow at once. 0 removes the glass look. The per-state switches decide where glass appears; this decides how strong.*
Sheen strength *The white highlight band only. Lower this if glass looks washed out rather than tinted. 0 removes the sheen but keeps the rims.*
Sheen direction *Which way the highlight band runs. Separate from each state's tint gradient.*

Stop flicker on window focus *Zen greys out inactive windows and light-dark() colours re-resolve when focus changes. With transitions armed that animates every time you click away and back. This disables transitions only while the window is inactive.*

Snap into place at startup *Sine loads this mod's stylesheet from JavaScript, after the window has already drawn itself with Zen's defaults. Button and font sizes therefore arrive a moment late, and because those properties are animated, the correction slides visibly instead of just being there. This holds transitions off until startup settles, so it snaps once. It cannot remove the delay itself, only the animation of it.*
Selected tab
Style selected tabs *Independent switch. Everything below applies only to this state.*
Tint strength *How much source colour this state starts with.*
Opacity *Fades the whole tab including label and favicon.*
Gradient direction *Independent of every other state.*
Gradient end *What the gradient fades toward. Transparent shows whatever is behind. Weaker tint keeps the same hue at the End tint value. Second colour blends toward the Second gradient colour.*
End tint *Absolute strength at the far end. Only used by the weaker-tint and second-colour modes.*
Gradient spread *Where the fade finishes, across the tab. 100% is edge to edge; lower ends early and leaves a flat run.*
Glass sheen *The white highlight band.*
Glass rim *A 1px inner highlight along the top edge.*
Rim top highlight *Multiplier on the bright line along the selected tab's top edge. 1 is the current strength, 0 removes just that line and keeps the ring.*
Rim ring *Multiplier on the faint outline around the whole selected tab.*

Rim colour *The colour of the selected tab's rim itself. White is the glass default; any CSS colour works, and the strength rows above scale its alpha rather than replacing it. Try the accent colour for a tinted rim.*
Rim highlight edge *Which side of the selected tab carries the bright line. Ring only drops the line and keeps the outline.*
Rim highlight thickness *How thick the selected tab's bright line is. Above about 3px it reads as a band rather than a highlight.*
Rim ring thickness *How thick the outline around the selected tab is.*
Outer glow *A soft tinted halo. Replaces the rim shadow, so it includes the rim when both are on.*

Tabs, shared

Detailed rim control *Adds strength, fade and axis rows to each tab state's Rim light above. Every value is a multiplier or an option on the rim you already have, so nothing changes until you move one.*
Tab roundness *Corner radius. Arc rebinds Zen's --border-radius-medium; this overrides it for tabs only.*
Texture *An overlay pattern on every tab state. Plain CSS gradients, so the cost is one extra background layer.*
Accent bar on the selected tab *A 3px bar down the left edge. Replaces Arc's container glow, which uses the same layer.*

Keep the favicon while a page loads *Zen swaps the favicon for a spinner while a tab loads, and Firefox clears the icon when the load ends until the new page's favicon arrives; together they read as the icon blinking out and back. This hides the spinner, Zen's own switch, and keeps the last icon in place for as long as the tab stays on the same site, however slow the page. A different site never wears the previous icon.*
Hide Arc's container glow *Arc paints a blurred bar of container colour across the left half of every container tab. Usually the extra colour you see on the left.*

Close button on the left *Hovering a regular tab swaps its icon for the close button; pinned tabs keep their icon with the button beside it, and Essentials keep theirs. Replaces the Left close button mod.*
Hide the pinned-tabs separator *The line between pinned and regular tabs. Replaces Remove Tabs Separator. SuperPins' Show separator setting controls the same line, so set only one.*
Essentials favicon grows on hover *Pointing at an Essential enlarges its favicon, with a small spring.*
Tab strip
Gradient behind the whole strip *One wash across the whole sidebar, edge to edge, rather than per tab.*
Strip strength *How strong the wash is at its start.*
Strip direction *Independent of every other section.*
Sidebar
Hide back and forward *The arrows at the top of the sidebar, for a mouse with its own back and forward buttons. They return while customizing the toolbar. Replaces Back Fwd Always Hidden.*

Enable sidebar styling *Docked, the sidebar gets the tint gradient below. In compact mode Zen floats the sidebar over the page, and the floating panel gets the panel settings further down. Arc's compact sidebar section paints the same panel; turn Arc's blur and opacity down and let this own it.*
Sidebar tint *Docked sidebar only. 0% leaves the docked sidebar untouched; raise it for a workspace-coloured gradient behind it.*

Fill strength *Scales the tint's own transparency. This is NOT element opacity: fading the element would fade your tabs and text with it, which is what the old Opacity setting did. 1 is full strength, 0.5 is half.*
Sidebar gradient direction *Independent of every other section.*
Glass sheen on the sidebar *Independent switch.*
Glass rim on the docked sidebar *Docked only; the floating panel has its own border setting below.*
Floating panel (compact mode)
Panel colour *Neutral is Arc's plain dark glass: black or white with the theme, no colour. Workspace mixes the workspace colour in at the accent tint below. Custom mixes the colour you give.*
Custom panel colour *Any CSS colour.*
Panel border *Thin line is Arc's edge: one pixel, white at 15%. Glass rim is the same highlight-plus-line the tabs use, from the shared rim settings.*
Border colour *Any CSS colour, for the thin line.*
Border width *For the thin line.*
Panel gradient direction *Which way the floating panel's gradient runs.*

Panel gradient end *What the accent fades toward. Base keeps the panel's opacity and drops the colour. Weaker tint keeps the hue at the End tint value. Second colour blends toward the Second gradient colour.*
Panel end tint *Strength of the colour at the far end, for the weaker-tint and second-colour ends.*
Panel gradient spread *Where the fade finishes across the panel. 100% is edge to edge; lower ends early and leaves a flat run.*
Glass sheen on the panel *The same highlight the tabs use, over the panel gradient.*
Panel shadow *Zen's own drop shadow under the floating panel.*
Panel accent tint *How much of the panel colour is mixed into the base, for the Workspace and Custom colour modes. 10% is a hint; 25% and up visibly colours the glass.*
Panel corner radius *Rounding of the floating panel.*
Workspaces

Style the workspace switcher *The row of workspace icons at the bottom of the sidebar, in the same glass as the tabs and window buttons. Pointing at an icon moves only the icon, so nothing beside it shifts. While this is on, Arc 2.0's own workspace styles are switched off (Other mods).*
Background
Pointed at *The icon grows with a small spring and settles; Dock also lifts its neighbours a little. Only icons move, never the buttons.*
Other workspaces
Current workspace
Steady dots *With more workspaces than fit, Zen shrinks the others to dots and widens the one you point at, pushing its neighbours along. On, every dot keeps its width and shows its icon in place.*
Zen's blur

Zen's blur *Zen's own Acrylic elements switch: it blurs what is behind the compact sidebar, the floating toolbar and the urlbar. Off, Zen draws them solid; Customise Zen's blur below still blurs Glassflow's sidebar panel.*

Customise Zen's blur *Zen's acrylic blurs whatever is behind its compact sidebar and floating toolbar, and Glassflow's overlays and the other mods' glass use the same blur. Off keeps Zen's own values; on uses the four below for all of them.*
Blur strength *Zen uses 42px. Higher smears more; lower keeps shapes legible.*
Brightness *Zen uses 0.25, which keeps text readable over bright pages. Raise it to let more of the page through.*
Saturation *Zen uses 1.1. Raise it for richer colour through the glass; lower drains it.*
Contrast *Zen uses 1. Above 1 deepens what shows through, below 1 flattens it.*
Darken the sidebar's edges *A soft shade just inside the compact sidebar's edges, painted rather than blurred so it holds still while you hover.*
See-through sidebar
Panel opacity *How solid the floating panel's base is, as a percentage. 70% is the dark, defined look; 0% is see-through with only the tint.*
Workspace gradient through the panel *Zen paints the workspace gradient on the panel. 0 hides it for a clean dark panel; 1 lets it through, which reads lighter and hazier.*

Blur the page when the sidebar shows *Follows the sidebar exactly, with nothing to measure or line up, because it runs in the browser where the sidebar's state is known. It blurs the whole page rather than a strip -- a filter cannot be clipped to one region -- so it reads as the page receding while the sidebar is up. Turning this on disables the strip method below.*
Also when not in compact mode *A docked sidebar never covers the page, so this is purely a look: the page softens whenever the sidebar is hovered.*
Page blur radius *Small values read as depth; large values make the page unreadable while the sidebar is open, which some people want and some hate.*
Page saturation while blurred *1 leaves colour alone; below 1 drains it as the page recedes.*
Blur fade speed *How quickly the page softens and clears as the sidebar comes and goes.*
Overlays

Glass behind overlays *Glass blurred with Zen's own blur (Sidebar > Customise Zen's blur), for Zen's surfaces that float inside the window: the library's download stack (hover the library button), toasts, glance's side buttons and the library media preview. Zen fades the tabs out under the download stack; with this on they stay and show through blurred.*
Overlay fill *How much tint covers the blur. 0% is clear glass; 100% hides what is behind.*
Library download stack *Hover the library button. Off lets Zen fade the tabs out under it again.*

label: Menu and panel fill (Windows 11) *Menus and panels are separate windows, so only Windows can blur behind them. On Windows 11 22H2 and later Firefox turns on Windows' acrylic for them and Zen tints it 50%; lower shows more of the blur. No effect on Windows 10, or when Windows shows an accent colour on title bars with a custom inactive colour, because Firefox turns the acrylic off there.*

Music player fill *The media player at the bottom of the sidebar, whose title row floats over the tabs on hover. Any CSS colour; the default is the Overlay fill above. Which rows the player shows is set in Mediaflow.*

Glass status pill *The link address shown at the bottom of the page while hovering a link, as a floating pill of overlay glass. Replaces Floating Statusbar. Arc 2.0 also floats it; turn Arc's version off so only one styles it.*
Status pill glass *Behind the link address pill.*

label: Theme-coloured dialogs *Dialogs take the menu colour, and their main button the accent colour. Replaces Dialog Fix.*
Window buttons
Enable macOS-style traffic lights *Turn OFF Arc's own 'macOS style buttons' first.*
Position *Which end of the sidebar row the buttons sit on.*
Show colour at rest *Off: neutral grey until hovered.*
Vertical oval on hover *Only the button under the cursor stretches.*
Oval height on hover *A multiple of the diameter, applied on top of the Resting shape below. 1.3 with a resting height of 1.15 stretches further on hover; 1.0 cancels hover growth entirely.*

Resting width *Width as a multiple of the button's diameter, independent of height. 1.0 is normal width, 1.4 is noticeably wider, below 1.0 narrows it. Combine with Resting shape (height) for a capsule in either orientation.*

Resting shape *Height as a multiple of the width. 1.0 is a circle, 1.15 a subtle capsule, 1.4 clearly elongated. The corner curve stays fixed at half the button width, so taller values give flat sides with the same round caps rather than stretching into an ellipse.*

Width on hover *A multiple of the diameter, applied via a compositor transform so it cannot push the other buttons sideways. 1 means hover does not change width, matching Resting width means no change either. Try 1.3 for a button that widens rather than lengthens on hover.*
Show glyphs on hover *Triggered by hovering anywhere in the group, matching macOS.*
Glyph size *A fraction of the button's width. 0.62 is close to macOS. Renamed from the old percentage setting, because a stale percentage broke the sizing maths and made the marks vanish entirely.*
Button opacity *Fades buttons at rest. Hover restores full opacity.*
Glass sheen on buttons *Independent switch.*
Glass rim on buttons *Independent switch.*

Close colour *Proton purple-60, a jewel amethyst rather than a pastel. Any CSS colour works. Alpha near 0.78 keeps it readable as glass while staying saturated. Hover stacks a second pass to deepen it further.*
Minimise colour *Proton blue-60, a sapphire tone. Keep alpha around 0.75 to 0.85: lower washes out, higher stops reading as glass.*
Maximise colour *A deep emerald, replacing the pastel mint. Green is the one hue macOS already uses for zoom.*

When the window is not focused *Arc paints the stock red/yellow/green traffic lights on inactive windows, which is what was overriding your choices. All three options below restate your colours so Arc cannot leak through.*

On hover *Arc paints the stock red, yellow and green on plain hover. All three options restate your own colours so Arc cannot show through. Keep colour is the default: hovering no longer changes the hue at all.*
Hover intensity *1 means the colour does not change on hover at all, which is the default. Above 1 saturates further. This is separate from the hover fill below.*
Hover colour, close *Leave empty to deepen the resting colour instead. Set a colour here only if you want hover to shift hue rather than intensity.*
Hover colour, minimise *Leave empty to deepen the resting colour.*
Hover colour, maximise *Leave empty to deepen the resting colour.*
Diameter *macOS uses 12px, Arc uses 14px.*
Gap between buttons *macOS uses roughly 8px.*

Tidy system buttons *Spacing, Zen's rounded corners and a red close on hover for the normal minimise, maximise and close buttons. Only while the traffic lights above are off. Replaces TitleBarButton UI Tweaks.*
Corner shape

Turn squircles off browser-wide *Rounds menus, panels, dialogs and the URL bar, plus Glassflow and Groupflow surfaces set to Follow Zen. Explicit Corner shape choices still take precedence. Applies and reverts instantly, no restart.*

Corner shape *Zen 1.22b reshapes every corner in the browser with CSS `corner-shape: superellipse()` -- 1.3 on most platforms, 2.3 on Windows. `squircle` is superellipse(2), so Windows sits past it, heading toward square. That rule targets the universal selector, so it reshapes this mod's tabs and buttons too, and a radius you tuned before 1.22b now reads square. Follow Zen mirrors Zen, including Glassflow's Turn squircles off browser-wide setting. Round (classic) is superellipse(1) and restores exactly how these surfaces looked before 1.22b. Applies only to Glassflow's own surfaces; the rest of the browser keeps Zen's shape.*

Custom superellipse value *Used by every Custom superellipse option. 1 is a plain round corner, 2 is a squircle, higher goes squarer (Zen uses 2.3 on Windows), and negative values scoop the corner inward. `infinity` is a hard square.*

Radius source *Where the corner radius comes from. The number is Tab roundness under *Tabs, shared*. **Follow Zen's own corner radius** reads Zen's `--border-radius-medium` instead, which since 1.22b is already scaled for the squircle corner -- so these surfaces track Zen's design language through future restyles rather than drifting away from it the way a pinned number did when 1.22b landed. Leave Radius compensation Off when following Zen; Zen's token already carries that scaling, and applying it twice over-rounds.*

Radius compensation *A superellipse corner eats its radius differently from a circular one, so a radius tuned before Zen 1.22b reads tighter now. This scales every radius this mod sets, so you do not re-type each one. Auto uses the same factor Zen applies to its own corners, and it is per-platform, so Windows gets more than everywhere else without you typing a number. Turn this on first if tabs look square at a radius that used to look right; only reach for Custom if Auto overshoots.*
Custom radius multiplier *Only used when Radius compensation is set to Custom. 1 leaves radii alone; Zen compensates its own surfaces by roughly 2.1.*
Corner shape, tabs *Overrides the shape above for tab backgrounds only.*
Corner shape, Essentials *Overrides the shape above for Essentials cards only. They are far larger than a tab, so the same corner reads very differently on them.*

Corner shape, window buttons *Overrides the shape above for the traffic lights. Round is what makes them read as circles and capsules -- a superellipse at the same radius squares them off, which is the most visible place Zen 1.22b changed their look.*
Corner shape, sidebar *Overrides the shape above for the compact sidebar's rounded corner.*
Interface font
Set the interface font *Changes tab labels, menus and toolbar text. Never touches web pages. This box only changes the typeface. Font SIZE is a separate switch below.*

Font *Atkinson Hyperlegible Next is the current release and what the Braille Institute recommends: seven weights against the original's two, variable format, 150 languages, and a Mono cut. The extra weights matter here, because browser chrome uses several and the 2019 original forces the renderer to fake them. Entries marked for dyslexia follow the British Dyslexia Association style guide; the four marked 'ships with Windows' need no install. Free from Google Fonts, or brailleinstitute.org/freefont for Atkinson and opendyslexic.org for OpenDyslexic. An uninstalled font silently falls back to the system one.*

options.label: Comic Sans MS  -- dyslexia (ships with Windows)

label: Custom font family *Only used when Font is set to Custom. Type the family name exactly as installed, for example: Iosevka, Public Sans. Commas work as fallbacks. Not the same as Firefox Settings > Fonts, which only affects web page text.*
Letter spacing *Extra space between characters. The British Dyslexia Association recommends slightly increased tracking; 0.05em is a gentle lift, 0.12em is pronounced. Use 'normal' for none.*
Word spacing *Extra space between words. Roughly 0.16em is the usual accessibility suggestion. Use 'normal' for none.*
Line height *Mostly affects menus and multi-line labels rather than tab titles. 1.5 is the common accessibility recommendation. Use 'normal' for none.*
Interface font size

Set interface font sizes *Replaces the Customize Font Size mod: same four surfaces it covered (tab bar, workspace title, find bar, workspace icons), plus folders, the URL bar and menus. Turn OFF Customize Font Size if you enable this -- both target font-size on overlapping elements, and running both means whichever loads last quietly wins, whichever mod that turns out to be.*
Tab bar text size *Same element Customize Font Size calls 'Tabbar tabs'. Accepts em or px, for example 1.3em or 20px.*
Workspace title size *The current workspace's name, shown above the sidebar.*
Find bar text size *The in-page search bar, Ctrl+F.*

Workspace icon size *The workspace switcher icons at the bottom of the sidebar. CFS calls this an icon size but implements it as font-size, since the icons are glyphs; kept identical here for a clean replacement.*
Folder label size *Tab group names. Not covered by Customize Font Size.*
URL bar text size *Not covered by Customize Font Size.*
Menu text size *Right-click menus and dropdown panels. Not covered by Customize Font Size.*
Animation

Instant UI animations *Zen animates its interface -- tab open and close, workspace switches, folders -- through its bundled Motion library. This flips that library's global switch so every UI animation jumps straight to its final frame: the interface responds at input speed instead of animation speed. Applies and reverts live, and web pages are untouched. This is a look change by design; leave it off if you like the motion.*
Other mods

*Each row switches off another mod's settings that double up with something Glassflow or Groupflow draws, only while that part of ours is on, and only settings the other mod has written. Turning a row off, or our part off, puts back what was there; a setting you change by hand afterwards is left alone. Tab Unloader has the row for Arc's own tab unloading.*

Arc 2.0 *macOS-style buttons, while Glassflow's window buttons are on. Greyscale unloaded tabs, while the Unloaded tab state is on. Folder backgrounds and Arc's tab group styling, while Groupflow is on.*

Arc 2.0 blur and transparency *Its compact sidebar fill, while Glassflow's sidebar styling is on, and its custom menu opacity, while Glassflow's overlays are on (they set the same menu fill). Arc's compact sidebar blur needs nothing: Glassflow's Zen blur replaces it on the same panel.*
Arc 2.0 workspace icons *Its workspace icon style (set to Disable) while Glassflow styles the workspace switcher.*
Zen's unloaded-tab fade *browser.tabs.fadeOutUnloadedTabs, which Arc's settings also show. Off while the Unloaded tab state is on, since that sets its own opacity.*
SuperPins *Unloaded-tab dimming and strikethrough, while the Unloaded tab state is on.*
Sidebar Expand on Hover *Fade sleeping tabs, while the Unloaded tab state is on.*
Transparent Zen *Compact sidebar type set to Default while Zen's blur (acrylic) is on: Push and Mask leave nothing under the panel to blur.*
Troubleshooting

Outline what Glassflow touches *Magenta on tabs, cyan on window buttons. For the sidebar: orange is the whole sidebar, gold is the compact background, pink is the titlebar. Whichever outlines actually appear are the elements that exist in your layout, so pick that one as the Sidebar target.*
